As one, we Inspire brilliance
An award-winning independent day school for girls aged 4–18.
Guildford High School is an exceptional place of possibility. A place where pupils grow as brave, resilient learners, guided by kindness, happiness and a shared spirit of aiming high — flourishing, as one.
Inspiring Girls Since 1888
As one, we Ignite ambition
GHS girls are challenged to think BIG, push boundaries and strive for excellence in everything they do. They are encouraged to question, create and innovate — embracing challenges not as obstacles, but as opportunities. With curiosity, courage and confidence, they grow into resilient, forward-thinking leaders of the future, united in their ambition to make a positive impact on the world.

They are encouraged to question, create and innovate — embracing challenges not as obstacles, but as opportunities. With curiosity, courage and confidence, they grow into resilient, forward-thinking leaders of the future, united in their ambition to make a positive impact on the world.

As one, we Discover talents
Our expansive Academic Enrichment programme complements our knowledge-based curriculum. Pupils learn a range of skills through thematic sessions each week, that evolve as they progress through the school.
Clubs and trips
Learning is taken outside of the classroom through a wide range of clubs and trips. We encourage every pupil to try new things. Pupils develop resilience and the confidence to take appropriate risks.
Our expansive Academic Enrichment programme complements our knowledge-based curriculum. Pupils learn a range of skills through thematic sessions each week, that evolve as they progress through the school.
The range and quality of extra-curricular activities are excellent, with opportunities for further learning in an abundant choice of pursuits.
Hit your stride
Sport is an extremely important and popular part of school life. We strive to encourage everyone to participate and enjoy sporting activity, whether for competition, fitness, health or purely for fun and recreation. Pupils enjoy a variety of sports within their timetabled PE lessons and our outstanding sports facilities are also used to their full advantage for extra-curricular sporting activities.
They are one of the most successful sporting girls’ schools in the country – and continue to be year after year.
Unlock your sound
Pupils at Guildford High School are passionate about music and we create numerous opportunities for participation and performance for musicians of all ability levels. The recent opening of a dedicated performing arts building has created a state-of-the-art centre in which students can develop their musical talents.
Being part of the brass band is so special. The feeling of everybody having a shared passion is amazing.
Take centre stage
Rehearsals run nearly year-round for our next highly anticipated production, staged in the main hall, drama hall, or drama studio. All productions are supported by our very own pupil tech crews who look after sound and lighting. Pupils also take the lead as set designers, costume designers and of course our own talented musicians provide all instrumental support.
School productions foster teamwork and inspire commitment from every pupil, whether on stage or contributing their skills behind the scenes.
As one, we Care and thrive
Together, our exceptional teaching staff and pupils work together to create a happy, close-knit and supportive school community. Kindness and consideration for others is an everyday part of school life.
ASPIRE programme
In the Senior School our ASPIRE programme addresses the issues which young people face as they grow up in today’s world.
Wellbeing week
Our annual ‘Wellbeing Week’ is an established highlight of the school calendar and last year featured yoga, circus skills, a silent disco and hot chocolate walks.
Together, our exceptional teaching staff and pupils work together to create a happy, close-knit and supportive school community. Kindness and consideration for others is an everyday part of school life.
Extraordinary staff
Our staff are integral to delivering high quality education to the girls in our care, inspiring them to think and learn creatively.
We devote energy and commitment to our pastoral care.

KS3 perform The Wolves of Willoughby Chase
Our Years 7–9 Drama students took to the stage with a brilliant production of The Wolves of Willoughby Chase , a fast-paced, fun and frantic adventure set in an alternative history of England, following two brave girls as they battled ferocious wolves, snowy wastelands and their evil guardian, Miss Slighcarp. Based on Joan Aiken’s 1962 children’s novel, the story blended the fictional nineteen-century in which the story was originally set with a 1980s twist.
A huge well done to all the talented performers and stage crew involved.

Student Article Published in Spanish Magazine
We are very proud of Emma, a GHS Lower Sixth student, who has had her writing published in Sobremesa, a Spanish magazine published by King’s College London. KCL’s Department of Languages, Literatures and Cultures took submissions from Year 12 and 13 students all across the country, and entrants were invited to consider the question ‘What will a Spanish or Latin American city be like in 100 years?’, with submissions taking the form of a text which explores what society, culture, traditions and festivals, customs, landscapes, people, or technology will be like a century from now. Emma’s clever and creative article was selected from a large number of submissions – congratulations, Emma!

Drama
With over ten dramatic productions per year, there are almost always rehearsals underway in the Drama department at GHS.
From large-scale musicals and major plays to smaller showcases that celebrate creativity and collaboration across year groups, pupils take part in a vibrant programme of drama productions. Highlights include our biennial whole-school musical, year-group performances such as the Year 7 Pantomime (written and directed by the Sixth Form), the Year 8 Shakespeare Festival, and other student-led shows that bring the school community together.
Drama at GHS
Our dedicated performing arts centre provides outstanding rehearsal and teaching spaces. Productions take place in our main hall as well as the drama hall or drama studio. As well as performing on the stage, there are a multitude of opportunities for pupils to perform behind the scenes. All productions are supported by our very own pupil tech crews who look after sound and lighting. Pupils also take the lead as set designers, costume designers and of course our own talented musicians provide all instrumental support. As our photos illustrate, the standard of production is incredibly high.
Productions foster a great sense of teamwork and require commitment and enthusiasm from pupils, whether they are taking a leading role on stage or contributing their skills as part of the technical crew.
Ms Ashley Fenton, Director of Drama
All pupils in Years 7 and 8 enjoy a weekly Drama lesson as part of the curriculum. Pupils in Year 9 choose to continue with curriculum Drama lessons. Oracy lessons have also been introduced for younger pupils in the Senior School. GCSE Drama is popular with around 25 pupils choosing it as an option each year and generally 10 pupils will wish to continue through to A-level. Sixth Form students form a professional-standard company, The Morton Players, who perform at Edinburgh Festival Fringe. Recent leavers have gone on to win places at prestigious institutions such as RADA.

Music
Music is integral to day-to-day life at GHS. The practice rooms in our dedicated performing arts building are filled with the sounds of learning in action, with peripatetic lessons ranging from flute to guitar, piano to percussion.
Pupils here are passionate about music, and we create numerous opportunities for participation and performance for musicians of all ability levels. Instrumental lessons take place each week and there are five choirs, including three large choirs for all-comers and auditioned Chamber Choirs for the most able singers. Pupils can audition for the Symphony Orchestra, Chamber Orchestra and Wind Band (Grade 5 / 6 standard and above), while the String Orchestra and Mathias Band offers ensemble opportunities for less experienced instrumentalists. Over 30 ensembles, such as the Big Band, Brass, Guitar, Clarinet and Flute Ensembles, meet each week and perform at concerts. Pupils learn in a state-of-the-art centre where they can develop their musical talents and bring their creativity to life.
Music fills our corridors before, during and after school. It is part of the fabric of GHS life.
Music at GHS
A lively programme of events includes informal and major concerts at school, instrumental support to all school musicals, performances including at venues such as Westminster Abbey and St Paul’s Cathedral, an annual European music tour as well as annual highlights such as the Carol Service at Guildford Cathedral.
All pupils enjoy a weekly music lesson as part of the Year 7-9 curriculum, instrumental lessons take place in our many dedicated practice rooms and larger ensembles enjoy use of our purpose built performance venue, the recital hall and the performing arts centre.

Partnerships
At the heart of all partnership work, both in school life and beyond, are relationships. Our time spent getting to know one another understanding goals and challenges, finding common ground, helps us to identify how we can work together. At GHS we are focused on building relationships with our local schools and community organisations; it is these that underpin all our partnership work.
We work closely with many nearby schools and are a founding member of the West Surrey Partnership, a cross-sector, cross-phase partnership that includes over 25 schools in and around Guildford. This collaboration enriches the learning experience for students and staff across all our schools.
Community
We are committed to being an active member of our local community. From hosting events and workshops that welcome students, families and staff from surrounding areas to providing opportunities for mutual learning and growth.
Our community initiatives are designed to bring people together, bridging differences and building on our shared commitment to growth and understanding.
Charities
Guildford High School is passionate about supporting local charities and creating opportunities for students to make a positive impact in their community. Since 2020, we have developed a strong relationship with the Guildford Community Wellbeing Team based at The Hive, an organisation dedicated to supporting vulnerable families in our area. Our students have taken the lead in organising Christmas collections, run regular drives to support the local Hygiene Bank and Food Bank. Most recently, our students collected and donated Easter eggs for children at both The Hive and Cherry Trees, a local charity which supports children with complex disabilities.

Academic Enrichment
Alongside our knowledge-based curriculum, all Senior School pupils benefit from a rich skills-based curriculum designed to broaden horizons, deepen curiosity, and nurture the confidence needed for life beyond the classroom. Academic enrichment is a dedicated weekly slot for every year group, providing structured opportunities to think differently, explore new ideas and develop essential skills.
Academic enrichment evolves as pupils progress through the school, but remains centred on developing the whole person. Sessions draw on the expertise of our teachers and visiting speakers, and focus on themes such as:
Public speaking and oracy
Metacognition and effective study skills
Exposure to new and unfamiliar ideas
Current affairs and global awareness
Research and independent inquiry
Creativity, collaboration and problem-solving
Encouraging intellectual curiosity
Throughout the year, pupils engage in thought-provoking activities, debates, workshops and lectures that encourage them to question, analyse and make connections between the world they know and the one they are discovering. Recent sessions have explored topics such as:
Interdisciplinary links between Biology, Design and Engineering
Developing critical thinkers
In Years 7-9, all pupils complete an independent research project, which helps them develop critical thinking, resilience and academic curiosity through guided enquiry and structured support.
Academic enrichment is an integral part of school life at GHS – designed to stretch thinking, deepen interest and build the skills for life that sit proudly alongside our rigorous academic curriculum.

Academic Ethos
Our pupils across the whole ability range prove to themselves routinely that there are very few limits to what they can achieve. We are immensely proud of the academic achievements of every single one of our pupils. We recognise and celebrate the different strengths and interests of all our pupils and we do not compare them.
Our goal is to help all of our pupils to achieve their best and to fulfil their own personal potential.
We seek to nurture in all our pupils their innate intellectual curiosity and love of learning. This starts with the outstanding teaching, guidance and support of our teaching staff, who pass on to pupils their passion for their subject and for learning for its own sake. The curriculum is broad and varied; curriculum content is highly rigorous and carefully considered to ensure that pupils learn the richest, most inspiring knowledge and the most essential skills in each subject. There is an emphasis on creativity, which thrives when pupils have the opportunity to use the knowledge and skills that they have acquired in imaginative ways. Voluntary reading groups, trips and visits, internal and external essay competitions, challenges, Olympiads and lectures by outside speakers are a regular and hugely popular feature of school life.
The learning environment is hugely supportive and collaborative, and this is a key to success: all pupils are ambitious, curious and interested in their work and they relish learning with like-minded peers, and are exceptionally adept at exchanging and developing ideas. This collaboration can be seen in every lesson and in the huge array of activities beyond the classroom in which pupils participate.
Technology plays an important role in enhancing teaching and learning, and in ensuring excellent preparation of our pupils for an increasingly digital world. All pupils use an iPad and Apple Pencil which enables the use of well-integrated digital technologies to enhance learning, allowing our students to work collaboratively and creatively, in a way that is at once more connected and more personalised.
By seizing opportunities to find their intellectual passions in a supportive, collaborative environment, our pupils acquire the confidence to take risks, to play with ideas and to let their voices be heard.
Alongside the curriculum, time is dedicated each week in all year groups to academic enrichment. This serves firstly to expose pupils to academic topics from a wide range of domains beyond the curriculum, which may develop into deeper interests; and secondly to allow for the explicit development of skills such as oracy, critical thinking, problem-solving and research skills, and all pupils in Key Stage 3 undertake an independent research project. The aim is to ensure that our pupils have the complete package of knowledge, skills and attitudes to learning to ensure that they can take their place in the world after GHS, and indeed shape it.
Our Curriculum
Years 7-9
Throughout Years 7-9, the curriculum is broad, stimulating and exciting, and aims to expose pupils to a broad range of subjects to allow them find their passions. Maths is the only subject taught in ability sets (from January of Year 7); Biology, Chemistry and Physics are learned separately from Year 7; pupils learn either French or German in depth in Year 7 and then add a second modern language in Year 8 (French, German or Spanish); Geography, History, Religious Education, Latin, Computer Science, and Design & Technology are all learned throughout Key Stage 3; Art, Drama and Music are all learned in Years 7 and 8 and then two from the three are chosen in Year 9. One period per week is spent learning Philosophy in Year 7 and Natural History in Year 9, and there is one period a week of PSHE and four of PE/Games. Throughout Key Stage 3 the homework burden is relatively light, and no homework is set in the first fortnight of Year 7, in the school holidays or in the run-up to summer exams.
I love that every week feels different — whether we’re acting in Drama or doing experiments in Science, there’s always something new to get excited about.”
GCSE studies
For Years 10 and 11, pupils study either nine or ten GCSEs, not including Further Maths, which is taken in addition to GCSE Maths by pupils in a top Maths set (approximately 50% of the cohort). All pupils take Maths, English Language and Literature and either three separate Sciences or Double Award Science. In all but exceptional circumstances, all pupils must take at least one modern or classical language and at least one humanity (History, Geography or Religious Studies). Beyond these stipulations, any combination of subjects is possible. Pupils are strongly encouraged to continue to pursue a wide range of extracurricular activities, to maintain breadth and balance in their lives.

Articulation prize London finals
We are very proud of Lily (Lower Sixth) who spoke at the London Finals of the Articulation Prize, held at the V&A. After winning the Regional Finals earlier in the year, Lily returned to the competition to speak in the beautiful Lydia and Manfred Gorvy Lecture Theatre on the artwork ‘For, in Your Tongue, I Cannot Fit’ by Shilpa Gupta. This was a tough round to be selected to go on to the Grand Finals at the National Gallery – Lily spoke beautifully and placed third in these finals.
The competition was judged by Nicole-Rachelle Moore, a writer, educator and the Curator of Caribbean Collections at the British Library. She described the overall quality of the presentations as stellar, calling the experience “an exhilarating learning experience” and thanking all the speakers for sharing their work. Nicole-Rachelle Moore noted that she greatly enjoyed Lily’s presentation – she admired how Lily began by sharing how she first encountered the artwork, immediately engaging the audience, and she also praised the way Lily placed the work within a wider context, particularly her reflections on dignity and strength in resisting being silenced.
Huge congratulations to Lily for her wonderful speech. All photos from this event are © Hydar Dewachi.

Guildford High School Celebrates a Historic Year of Oxbridge Offers
Guildford High School is delighted to celebrate an exceptional year of university success, with pupils receiving a record 27 offers from Oxford and Cambridge — the highest number in the school’s history. This includes 10 offers from Oxford and 17 from Cambridge, reflecting the ambition and academic strength of the Upper Sixth.
Across the cohort, students have already secured over 320 offers from top universities on over 150 different courses, with many more decisions still to come. Highlights include 100% offer rates at York and Loughborough, 98% at Exeter, and strong outcomes at Bristol, Leeds, Bath and Nottingham.
This year has also seen significant international interest, with pupils applying to universities in the United States, Hong Kong, Sweden and Australia, and already receiving early offers and scholarships from prestigious global institutions.
Pupils’ academic commitment is further reflected in outstanding EPQ results, with 57 A* and 7 A grades, many of which contributed to reduced university offers.
We are immensely proud of the hard work and aspiration shown by our Upper Sixth pupils and look forward to celebrating further successes as the UCAS cycle continues.

Guildford High School named Southeast Independent Secondary School of the Year 2026
Guildford High School is delighted to have been named Independent Secondary School of the Year in the Southeast in this year’s Parent Power listings by The Sunday Times. Parent Power identifies the 2,000 highest-achieving schools in the UK based on examination results and overall school experience. In the published league table, Guildford High School ranks fifth nationally, and is the top performing girls’ school in the Southeast.
Helen Davies, editor of The Sunday Times Parent Power Guide, commented:
As well as celebrating the academic excellence of the top schools it is uplifting to see how they are shaping their students to be ready for the 21st century, and instilling a lifelong love of learning.
Commenting on the award, Karen Laurie, Head, said:
It is an honour to be named Independent School of the Year in the Southeast. Guildford High School creates an environment in which girls are happy, resilient and confident that they can realise their ambitions. This award celebrates both our place at the top of the league table and the school ethos that underpins this success.
Achieving individual and school success at such a high level is down to the holistic education that GHS provides. Together, our outstanding pupils and staff form a community that embraces all aspects of school life. Through our nurturing pastoral care programme, inspiring teaching, and wealth of co-curricular activities, we equip our pupils with the knowledge, skills, attitudes and values that enable them to thrive now and in the future.
Guildford High School has consistently earned national recognition through The Sunday Times Parent Power listings, ranking among the top ten schools in the country for the past 16 consecutive years. The school’s recent accolades include Independent School of the Year 2024, Southeast Independent School of the Year for Academic Performance in both 2023 and 2024, and Southeast Independent School of the Year 2022. The school has also been distinguished as Southeast Secondary School of the Decade and overall Prep School of the Decade.

Sport
Sport is an extremely important and popular part of school life. We strive to encourage all pupils to participate and enjoy a wide variety of sporting activity, whether for competition, fitness, health or purely for fun and recreation.
The PE department consists of specialist teachers and coaches who have the highest credentials, often having played at national level themselves. We are regularly ranked in the top three schools for sporting attainment in the national School Sport magazine, with our 2025 ranking being the Top Girls’ School for Sport.
During timetabled lessons, pupils in Years 7 and 8 enjoy athletics, cricket, dance, gymnastics, lacrosse, netball, swimming and tennis. The curriculum broadens for older pupils and we provide a host of other curricular and extra-curricular activities.
Our top performing athletes are supported through our Aspiring Athletes programme. This tailored initiative gives guidance and practical assistance to pupils managing elite sporting commitments alongside their studies. We currently have 55 athletes on national pathways across 12 different sports.
They are one of the most successful sporting girls' schools in the country - and continue to be year after year.
GHS Sport
Sporting facilities
Our purpose-built sports centre, located just 150 metres from the main school campus, reflects Guildford High School’s dedication to fostering sporting excellence. Designed to inspire athletic achievement and promote a healthy, active lifestyle, it serves as a vibrant hub for students, supporting a wide range of activities throughout the school community.
The GHS sports centre boasts an impressive range of facilities, including:
Competition-standard swimming pool
A six-lane, 25-metre pool, perfect for training, lessons, and competitive events.
Versatile sports hall
A full-size, multi-purpose space supporting a variety of indoor sports and activities.
Lacrosse pitches
Professional-grade pitches tailored to meet the demands of this fast-paced sport.
Modern fitness suite
A fully equipped gym with exercise machines, weights and fitness tools.
Netball courts
Five courts designed for practice and matches.
Outdoor tennis courts
Six courts available for lessons, training, and competitions.
Guildford Spectrum Athletics Stadium
Athletics training, competitions and sports days take place at Guildford Spectrum athletics stadium.
Comprising a 400m, eight lane international standard track and full complement of field facilities, it is a fantastic venue for our events.

Extended sporting grounds
The sports centre’s unique location, adjacent to Stoke Park, provides an invaluable extension to our sporting facilities. During term time, we utilize this expansive green space for additional marked pitches, cross-country running, and outdoor activities. This direct access to the 130-acre park enriches our physical education programme and provides students with diverse sporting opportunities in a natural setting.
Nearby, Guildford Spectrum contains an ice-skating rink and all-weather athletics track. Surrey Sports Park, with its astro hockey pitches, lacrosse pitches, climbing wall and squash courts, is also used by our pupils on a weekly basis.

Guildford High School has a well-deserved reputation for outstanding attainment. Our teams achieve consistent success at all levels of competition, and we are privileged to see many pupils progress beyond school level, achieving district, county and national representative honours in a wide variety of sports, from netball to gymnastics.

Wellbeing
Pupils learn best when they are happy, and we have carefully created an environment at GHS where pupils feel safe to push their boundaries and challenge themselves.
To ensure that they lead happy and fulfilling lives we teach our pupils to be kind to themselves and others, reinforcing the importance of reaching out for support when needed. Wellbeing events happen throughout the year and our annual ‘Wellbeing Week’ is an established highlight of the school calendar, which last year featured yoga, circus skills, a silent disco and hot chocolate walks.
Wellbeing at GHS is not an add-on, it is embedded into the curriculum and into the fabric of school life. The strength of our pastoral care is reflected in the culture of kindness that is apparent across the school and in how pupils treat each other.
Our Pastoral team
Our pastoral team is led by Mrs Catherine Gilmore, Deputy Head Pastoral. Mrs Gilmore’s dynamic leadership has resulted in a holistic approach to wellbeing, and she is supported by our experienced Heads of Year, form tutors, nursing team, school doctor and school counsellor. Core members of this team are based in our wellbeing hub and are always available for pupils to come and talk to throughout the day.
Trust is earned through good communication, connections and positive relationships between staff, pupils and parents. The pupil-teacher relationship is key to enabling all pupils to feel valued and cared for. Pupils know that they are believed in and can reach out for support. Form tutors give our pupils those day-to-day moments of care and support and are the first port of call for parental concerns or information regarding pastoral or academic matters. Heads of Year have overall responsibility for the pupils in their year group, creating a sense of community and belonging for their pupils.
However, our pastoral care goes beyond this core team. Every member of staff plays a role in supporting pupils and helping them thrive and every teacher is a teacher of wellbeing.
GHS is one big community where everyone is supportive of each other. We really care about each other.
ASPIRE programme
Our ASPIRE (Agency, Safety, Positivity, Inclusivity, Relationships and Economy) pastoral programme addresses the issues which young people face as they grow up in today’s world. We dedicate a lesson to this each week for every pupil. These lessons, along with assemblies and the curriculum, address the importance of ‘The GHS 8’ (our school values): being brave, kind, curious, taking risks and the importance of being part of an inclusive community.
Year 7 are taught positive life values and are taught how these shape character and influence well-being. Gratitude, respect, empathy, tolerance, courage and resilience are just some of the values that are understood in lessons and celebrated in the wider school community. Year 8 begin the year with a theatre trip to ‘Wicked’, which launches the theme of friendship and Year 9 learn the importance of self-esteem in making good choices, self-compassion and having a positive sense of self. Keeping safe, risk taking and reputation, money matters, female health, consent and the party scene are discussed as pupils move through school. Older pupils take part in a series of lessons preparing them for life after school, including budgeting, cooking, first aid, student loans and travel.
ASPIRE constantly adapts to meet the changing needs of our pupils, reacting to social trends and equipping pupils with the skills they need now, and in the future, to make informed, safe and healthy choices.
Working with parents
We approach wellbeing as an act of collaboration with parents as well as pupils. Our biennial pastoral conference is open to parents with pupils in school and those living locally. The event is delivered through keynote talks and workshops run by experts in their field.
The conference has given me a whole new, open and practical way to respond to my teenager.
SEND provision
We welcome all learners and are committed to every pupil achieving her full potential. We are well equipped to work with pupils who are neurodivergent, including those with ADHD, autism and dyslexia. We have a dedicated SEND hub in school which provides a calming space for pupils.
Dr Kerry Goodworth is our Assistant Head (SENDCo) and works with pupils and parents to put personal processes and support systems in place. All teaching staff are trained to teach to additional needs as standard, and value-added progress for pupils with additional needs matches that of the wider school.
